005package org.wpilib.command3;
006
007import static org.wpilib.util.ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam;
008
009import java.util.ArrayList;
010import java.util.List;
011import java.util.Set;
012import java.util.function.BooleanSupplier;
013import java.util.function.Supplier;
014import org.wpilib.annotation.NoDiscard;
015import org.wpilib.annotation.PostConstructionInitializer;
016
017/**
018 * A declarative state machine that can be used to implement complex command routines. State machine
019 * setup should be done in stages: first, a state machine is created and its name is set; second,
020 * states are added to the state machine using {@link #addState(Command)}; third, transitions
021 * between states can be specified using {@link State#switchTo(State)}:
022 *
023 * <pre>{@code
024 * // Declare the state machine
025 * StateMachine stateMachine = new StateMachine("Example State Machine");
026 *
027 * // Declare states
028 * State state1 = stateMachine.addState(...);
029 * State state2 = stateMachine.addState(...);
030 * State state3 = stateMachine.addState(...);
031 *
032 * // Set initial state
033 * stateMachine.setInitialState(state1);
034 *
035 * // Declare transitions
036 * state1.switchTo(state2).when(...);
037 * state2.switchTo(state3).when(...);
038 * }</pre>
039 *
040 * <p>Every state in a state machine runs a single command. While a state's command is running, the
041 * state machine will continually check all transitions that can be triggered from that state. If a
042 * transition is triggered, the state machine will cancel the state's command and move to the next
043 * state as defined by that transition. If no transition is triggered by the time the command
044 * completes, the state machine will exit unless a {@link
045 * TransitionNeedsConditionStage#whenComplete()} transition was specified from that state:
046 *
047 * <pre>{@code
048 * // switch from state1 to state2 when foo is true
049 * state1.switchTo(state2).when(() -> foo == true);
050 *
051 * // but if foo never becomes true, switch to state3 when state1 finishes
052 * state1.switchTo(state3).whenComplete();
053 *
054 * // no transitions are defined from state2 or state3,
055 * // so the state machine will exit when either state completes
056 * }</pre>
057 */
058public final class StateMachine implements Command {
059  private final String m_name;
060  private State m_initialState = null;
061  private final List<State> m_states = new ArrayList<>();
062
063  /**
064   * Creates a new state machine.
065   *
066   * @param name The name of the state machine. Cannot be null. This will appear in telemetry as the
067   *     {@link Command#name() name} of the state machine.
068   */
069  public StateMachine(String name) {
070    requireNonNullParam(name, "name", "StateMachine");
071    m_name = name;
072  }
073
074  @Override
075  public String name() {
076    return m_name;
077  }
078
079  @Override
080  public Set<Mechanism> requirements() {
081    // The machine itself doesn't have any requirements. Commands bound to the various states that
082    // the machine moves through may have requirements, however.
083    return Set.of();
084  }
085
086  /**
087   * Adds a new state to the state machine. State transitions can be specified on the new state
088   * using {@link State#switchTo(State)}.
089   *
090   * @param command The command for the state to execute. Cannot be null.
091   * @return The newly created state.
092   */
093  @NoDiscard
094  public State addState(Command command) {
095    requireNonNullParam(command, "command", "StateMachine.addState");
096    var state = new State(this, command);
097    m_states.add(state);
098    return state;
099  }
100
101  /**
102   * Sets up a transition from any of the given states to a specific state. If no states are given,
103   * the transition will apply to all states in the state machine <i>at the time this method is
104   * called</i>.
105   *
106   * <pre>{@code
107   * stateMachine.switchFromAny(state1, state2, state3).to(state4).when(() -> foo == true);
108   *
109   * // Functionally equivalent to:
110   * state1.switchTo(state4).when(() -> foo == true);
111   * state2.switchTo(state4).when(() -> foo == true);
112   * state3.switchTo(state4).when(() -> foo == true);
113   *
114   * // Set up an early exit condition from any state
115   * stateMachine.switchFromAny().toExitStateMachine().when(() -> bar == true);
116   *
117   * // Functionally equivalent to:
118   * state1.exitStateMachine().when(() -> bar == true);
119   * state2.exitStateMachine().when(() -> bar == true);
120   * state3.exitStateMachine().when(() -> bar == true);
121   * state4.exitStateMachine().when(() -> bar == true);
122   * }</pre>
123   *
124   * @param states The states to transition from.
125   * @return A builder for the transition.
126   */
127  public TransitionNeedsTargetStage switchFromAny(State... states) {
128    if (states.length == 0) {
129      return new TransitionNeedsTargetStage(List.copyOf(m_states));
130    } else {
131      return new TransitionNeedsTargetStage(List.of(states));
132    }
133  }
134
135  /**
136   * Sets the initial state for the state machine. This must be called before the state machine is
137   * scheduled. Failure to do so will result in an {@link IllegalStateException} being thrown when
138   * the state machine is started. Usage of this method is enforced by the WPILib compiler plugin;
139   * creating a state machine and neglecting to call this method will result in a compilation error.
140   *
141   * @param initialState The new initial state. Cannot be null.
142   * @see PostConstructionInitializer
143   */
144  @PostConstructionInitializer
145  public void setInitialState(State initialState) {
146    requireNonNullParam(initialState, "initialState", "StateMachine.setInitialState");
147    if (!this.equals(initialState.m_stateMachine)) {
148      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cannot set initial state in a different state machine");
149    }
150    m_initialState = initialState;
151  }
152
153  @Override
154  public void run(Coroutine coroutine) {
155    if (m_initialState == null) {
156      throw new IllegalStateException(
157          m_name + " does not have an initial state. Use .setInitialState() to provide one.");
158    }
159
160    var currentState = m_initialState;
161
162    outer_loop:
163    while (currentState != null) {
164      final var currentCommand = currentState.command();
165      // NOTE: The state machine will exit if the child command fails to be forked. This happens
166      //       if the command shares requirements with a higher-priority command.
167      coroutine.fork(currentCommand);
168      currentState.runEnterCallbacks();
169      boolean didYield = false;
170
171      while (coroutine.scheduler().isRunning(currentCommand)) {
172        for (var transition : currentState.transitions()) {
173          if (transition.shouldTransition()) {
174            // Cancel the current state's command and move to the next state specified by the
175            // transition. Break the state loop early to avoid an unnecessary yield() call and
176            // allow the next state's command to start in the same loop iteration that the
177            // previous state completed. If the next state is null, the state machine will exit
178            // immediately.
179            // Note: to prevent infinite loops when states transition to themselves, we require
180            // the transition signal to be a rising edge on the user-supplied condition to ensure
181            // that the transition is only triggered once per loop iteration.
182            currentState.runExitCallbacks();
183            coroutine.scheduler().cancel(currentCommand);
184            currentState = verifyState(transition.nextState());
185            continue outer_loop;
186          }
187        }
188
189        // Yield after checking all transitions.
190        // Note: this will be skipped if a transition is triggered.
191        coroutine.yield();
192        didYield = true;
193      }
194
195      // Move to the next configured state if no transition was hit before the command completed.
196      // We need to be careful about states with oneshot commands; they will complete immediately
197      // in the `fork()` call above and never enter the `while` loop and thus never yield.
198      // Therefore, we inject a yield call at the end here to ensure that the state machine will
199      // always yield once per state. This has a downside of adding extra loop cycles to states that
200      // may not need them (and has slightly different behavior to SequentialCommandGroup, which
201      // runs commands as fast as possible).
202      currentState.runExitCallbacks();
203      currentState = verifyState(currentState.nextState());
204      if (!didYield && currentState != null) {
205        // No need to yield if we're exiting the state machine
206        coroutine.yield();
207      }
208    }
209  }
210
211  private State verifyState(State next) {
212    if (next == null || this.equals(next.m_stateMachine)) {
213      // OK
214      return next;
215    }
216
217    // Bad user setup
218    throw new IllegalStateException(
219        "The next state does not belong to this state machine. Check the state for "
220            + next.command().name());
221  }
222
223  /**
224   * A state in a state machine. Each state has a command that will be run when it is active. States
225   * can transition to other states when some condition is met when that state is active, or
226   * automatically transition to another state when it completes if no transition conditions were
227   * met. A state with no transitions will never transition to another state, and will cause the
228   * state machine to exit when the state completes; likewise, a state with no incoming transitions
229   * will never be active.
230   */
231  public static final class State {
232    /** The state machine that this state belongs to. */
233    private final StateMachine m_stateMachine;
234
235    /** The command that will run when this state is active. */
236    private final Command m_command;
237
238    /** The possible states to transition to when this state completes. */
239    private final List<Completion> m_completions = new ArrayList<>();
240
241    /** The state to transition to by default when this state completes. May be null. */
242    private Supplier<State> m_defaultNextState = () -> null;
243
244    /**
245     * The transitions that can be triggered from this state. If multiple transitions are triggered
246     * at once, the first transition in the list will be used.
247     */
248    private final List<Transition> m_transitions = new ArrayList<>();
249
250    private final List<Runnable> m_enterCallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
251    private final List<Runnable> m_exitCallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
252
253    private State(StateMachine stateMachine, Command command) {
254      m_stateMachine = stateMachine;
255      m_command = command;
256    }
257
258    private Command command() {
259      return m_command;
260    }
261
262    private List<Transition> transitions() {
263      return m_transitions;
264    }
265
266    private void addTransition(Transition transition) {
267      m_transitions.add(transition);
268    }
269
270    /**
271     * Sets the next state to transition to when this state completes without having fired a
272     * transition first, or if no conditional completion transition has been met.
273     *
274     * @param nextState A supplier for the next state to transition to. Cannot be null, but may
275     *     return null.
276     */
277    private void setNextState(Supplier<State> nextState) {
278      m_defaultNextState = nextState;
279    }
280
281    // Custom boolean supplier classes may override .equals to do boolean value comparisons,
282    // particularly in Kotlin code. Check reference equality instead to just remove bindings to
283    // the same condition object.
284    @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
285    private void addCompletion(BooleanSupplier condition, Supplier<State> next) {
286      // Remove any preexisting completion with the same condition
287      m_completions.removeIf(c -> c.getCondition() == condition);
288      m_completions.add(new Completion(next, condition));
289    }
290
291    private State nextState() {
292      for (var completion : m_completions) {
293        if (completion.shouldTransition()) {
294          return completion.nextState();
295        }
296      }
297
298      // No conditional transition has been met, use the default next state.
299      // If this was never set or was set to be null, the state machine will exit.
300      return m_defaultNextState.get();
301    }
302
303    private void runEnterCallbacks() {
304      m_enterCallbacks.forEach(Runnable::run);
305    }
306
307    private void runExitCallbacks() {
308      m_exitCallbacks.forEach(Runnable::run);
309    }
310
311    /**
312     * Adds a function to be called when this state is entered. Callbacks are invoked immediately
313     * after the state's command is scheduled, and are run in the same order they were added.
314     *
315     * <p>Note: if a callback schedules any commands, those commands will be scoped to the lifetime
316     * of the entire state machine, <i>not</i> this state's lifetime.
317     *
318     * @param callback The callback to run. Cannot be null.
319     */
320    public void onEnter(Runnable callback) {
321      requireNonNullParam(callback, "callback", "State.onEnter");
322      m_enterCallbacks.add(callback);
323    }
324
325    /**
326     * Adds a function to be called when this state is exited. Callbacks are invoked immediately
327     * before the state's command is canceled, and are run in the order they were added. If the
328     * command finishes naturally, the callbacks are run immediately after it completes and before
329     * the next state is entered.
330     *
331     * @param callback The callback to run. Cannot be null.
332     */
333    public void onExit(Runnable callback) {
334      requireNonNullParam(callback, "callback", "State.onExit");
335      m_exitCallbacks.add(callback);
336    }
337
338    /**
339     * Starts building a transition to the specified state.
340     *
341     * @param to The state to transition to. Cannot be null.
342     * @return A builder for the transition.
343     */
344    public TransitionNeedsConditionStage switchTo(State to) {
345      requireNonNullParam(to, "to", "State.switchTo");
346      if (!m_stateMachine.equals(to.m_stateMachine)) {
347        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
348            "Cannot transition to a state in a different state machine");
349      }
350      return new TransitionNeedsTargetStage(List.of(this)).to(to);
351    }
352
353    /**
354     * Starts build a transition to some dynamic state. The supplier will be evaluated at the time
355     * the transition's condition is met.
356     *
357     * @param dynamic The dynamic state supplier. Cannot be null.
358     * @return A builder for the transition.
359     */
360    public TransitionNeedsConditionStage switchTo(Supplier<State> dynamic) {
361      requireNonNullParam(dynamic, "dynamic", "State.switchTo");
362      // Unfortunately, we can't check up front that the supplier will always return a state for
363      // this state machine. The output will need to be checked when the supplier is called
364      return new TransitionNeedsTargetStage(List.of(this)).to(dynamic);
365    }
366
367    /**
368     * Starts building a transition that will exit the state machine when triggered, rather than
369     * moving to a different state.
370     *
371     * @return A builder for the transition.
372     */
373    public TransitionNeedsConditionStage exitStateMachine() {
374      return new TransitionNeedsConditionStage(List.of(this), () -> null);
375    }
376  }
377
378  /**
379   * A builder for a transition from one state to another. Use {@link #to(State)} to specify the
380   * target state to transition to.
381   */
382  @NoDiscard("Use .to() to specify the target state")
383  public static final class TransitionNeedsTargetStage {
384    private final List<State> m_from;
385
386    private TransitionNeedsTargetStage(List<State> from) {
387      m_from = from;
388    }
389
390    /**
391     * Specifies the target state to transition to.
392     *
393     * @param to The state to transition to. Cannot be null.
394     * @return A builder to specify the transition condition.
395     */
396    public TransitionNeedsConditionStage to(State to) {
397      requireNonNullParam(to, "to", "NeedsTargetTransitionBuilder.to");
398      for (var state : m_from) {
399        if (!state.m_stateMachine.equals(to.m_stateMachine)) {
400          throw new IllegalArgumentException(
401              "Cannot transition to a state in a different state machine");
402        }
403      }
404      return new TransitionNeedsConditionStage(m_from, () -> to);
405    }
406
407    /**
408     * Specifies a dynamic target state to transition to. The supplier will be evaluated at the time
409     * the transition condition is met.
410     *
411     * @param dynamic A dynamic supplier for next states. Cannot be null.
412     * @return A builder to specify the transition condition.
413     */
414    public TransitionNeedsConditionStage to(Supplier<State> dynamic) {
415      requireNonNullParam(dynamic, "dynamic", "NeedsTargetTransitionBuilder.to");
416      return new TransitionNeedsConditionStage(m_from, dynamic);
417    }
418
419    /**
420     * Specifies the transition will exit the state machine when triggered, rather than moving to a
421     * different state.
422     *
423     * @return A builder to specify the transition condition.
424     */
425    public TransitionNeedsConditionStage toExitStateMachine() {
426      return new TransitionNeedsConditionStage(m_from, () -> null);
427    }
428  }
429
430  /**
431   * A builder to set conditions for a transition from one state to another. Use {@link
432   * #when(BooleanSupplier)} to make the transition occur when some external condition becomes true,
433   * or use {@link #whenComplete()} to make the transition occur when the originating state
434   * completes without having reached any other transitions first.
435   */
436  @NoDiscard("Use .when() or .whenComplete() to specify the transition condition")
437  public static final class TransitionNeedsConditionStage {
438    private final List<State> m_originatingStates;
439
440    // Note: A null result from the supplier indicates that the transition will cause the state
441    //       machine to exit
442    private final Supplier<State> m_targetStateSupplier;
443
444    private TransitionNeedsConditionStage(List<State> from, Supplier<State> to) {
445      requireNonNullParam(from, "from", "TransitionNeedsConditionStage");
446      requireNonNullParam(to, "to", "TransitionNeedsConditionStage");
447
448      m_originatingStates = from;
449      m_targetStateSupplier = to;
450    }
451
452    /**
453     * Adds a transition that will be triggered when the specified condition becomes true.
454     *
455     * <p><strong>NOTE: this had no effect if the originating state is a one-shot command without a
456     * yield.</strong> Use {@link #whenComplete()} instead for transitions from one-shot commands.
457     *
458     * <p>If multiple transitions are triggered in the same scheduler loop iteration, the first
459     * transition will fire and the rest will be ignored.
460     *
461     * <pre>{@code
462     * StateMachine stateMachine = new StateMachine("Example State Machine");
463     * State state1 = stateMachine.addState(...);
464     * State state2 = stateMachine.addState(...);
465     * State state3 = stateMachine.addState(...);
466     *
467     * state1.switchTo(state2).when(() -> foo == true);
468     *
469     * // never triggers because the first transition will be evaluated first
470     * state1.switchTo(state3).when(() -> foo == true);
471     * }</pre>
472     *
473     * @param condition The condition that will trigger the transition. Cannot be null.
474     */
475    public void when(BooleanSupplier condition) {
476      requireNonNullParam(condition, "condition", "NeedsConditionTransitionBuilder.when");
477      var transition = new Transition(m_targetStateSupplier, condition);
478      m_originatingStates.forEach(originatingState -> originatingState.addTransition(transition));
479    }
480
481    /**
482     * Adds a transition to the target state when the originating state completes without having
483     * triggered any other transitions first. If this is called multiple times for the same
484     * originating state, later calls will override the previous transitions. Any {@link
485     * #whenCompleteAnd} transitions will take precedence over {@code whenComplete} transitions if
486     * their conditions are met when the state exits.
487     *
488     * <pre>{@code
489     * StateMachine stateMachine = new StateMachine("Example State Machine");
490     * State state1 = stateMachine.addState(...);
491     * State state2 = stateMachine.addState(...);
492     * State state3 = stateMachine.addState(...);
493     *
494     * state1.switchTo(state2).whenComplete();
495     * state1.switchTo(state3).whenComplete(); // Overrides the previous transition
496     * state1.exitStateMachine().whenCompleteAnd(...); // Takes precedence if the condition is met
497     * }</pre>
498     */
499    public void whenComplete() {
500      m_originatingStates.forEach(state -> state.setNextState(m_targetStateSupplier));
501    }
502
503    /**
504     * Similar to {@link #when(BooleanSupplier)}, but only triggers when the originating state
505     * completes <i>and</i> some other condition is also met. {@code whenCompleteAnd} transitions
506     * will be evaluated in declaration order and take precedence over any {@link #whenComplete()}
507     * transitions that have been specified.
508     *
509     * <pre>{@code
510     * StateMachine stateMachine = new StateMachine("Example State Machine");
511     * State state1 = stateMachine.addState(...);
512     * State state2 = stateMachine.addState(...);
513     * State state3 = stateMachine.addState(...);
514     *
515     * state1.switchTo(state2).whenComplete();
516     * state1.switchTo(state3).whenComplete(); // Overrides the previous transition
517     * state1.exitStateMachine().whenCompleteAnd(...); // Takes precedence if the condition is met
518     * }</pre>
519     *
520     * @param condition The condition that will trigger the transition.
521     */
522    public void whenCompleteAnd(BooleanSupplier condition) {
523      requireNonNullParam(condition, "condition", "NeedsConditionTransitionBuilder.whenComplete");
524      m_originatingStates.forEach(state -> state.addCompletion(condition, m_targetStateSupplier));
525    }
526  }
527
528  /**
529   * Similar to {@link Transition}, but does not track the state of the condition. This is intended
530   * to only be checked once, when the originating state completes.
531   */
532  private static final class Completion {
533    private final Supplier<State> m_nextSupplier;
534    private final BooleanSupplier m_condition;
535
536    /**
537     * Creates a new completion object.
538     *
539     * @param next A supplier for the state to transition to when the originating state completes.
540     * @param condition The condition that will trigger the transition.
541     */
542    private Completion(Supplier<State> next, BooleanSupplier condition) {
543      m_nextSupplier = next;
544      m_condition = condition;
545    }
546
547    private boolean shouldTransition() {
548      return m_condition.getAsBoolean();
549    }
550
551    public State nextState() {
552      return m_nextSupplier.get();
553    }
554
555    public BooleanSupplier getCondition() {
556      return m_condition;
557    }
558  }
559
560  /**
561   * Similar to {@link Completion}, but tracks the state of the condition to avoid infinite loops.
562   * This is intended to be checked every loop while the originating state is active.
563   */
564  private static final class Transition {
565    /** The state to transition to. */
566    private final Supplier<State> m_nextSupplier;
567
568    /** The condition that will trigger the transition. */
569    private final BooleanSupplier m_condition;
570
571    private boolean m_previousSignal = false;
572
573    private Transition(Supplier<State> next, BooleanSupplier condition) {
574      m_nextSupplier = next;
575      m_condition = condition;
576    }
577
578    /** Checks if the transition should be triggered. */
579    private boolean shouldTransition() {
580      // Wrap the condition in a rising edge detector so that it will only trigger a single time per
581      // loop iteration. This prevents issues with a state transitioning to itself like so:
582      // state1.switchTo(state1).when(() -> foo == true);
583      // If the condition is itself a rising edge detector, this wrapping is redundant but harmless.
584      boolean currentValue = m_condition.getAsBoolean();
585      boolean isRisingEdge = currentValue && !m_previousSignal;
586      m_previousSignal = currentValue;
587      return isRisingEdge;
588    }
589
590    private State nextState() {
591      return m_nextSupplier.get();
592    }
593  }
594}
